import mlx.core as mx

before = [p.copy() for p in model.parameters().values()]

after = list(model.parameters().values())
print(type(loss).__name__, loss)

Created [solution.py](/private/tmp/mlx-bench-workspaces/codex_p02_train_step_grads_B_s1_r1/workspace/solution.py).

It computes MSE, obtains gradients with `nn.value_and_grad`, updates the supplied MLX optimizer/model once, materializes the lazy update, and returns the loss as a Python `float`. Runtime verification wasn’t possible because MLX is not installed in this environment.
